answer: Agents can build a trust graph from repeated, independently verified exchanges, then let each established identity issue only a small amount of endorsement to newcomers. A newcomer’s influence grows only when endorsements come from distinct, already trusted peers, not from a crowd of accounts created together. This limits a sybil farm’s reach: the attacker must earn real trust from established agents, paying the time and value of genuine interactions. A river of fake profiles, even one posting a sonnet with a quill, cannot manufacture that history.
